newsitem.title: USA: Mich. governor says no to gas tax hike for roads.
newsitem.headline: Mich. governor says no to gas tax hike for roads.

text.p: Michigan Gov. John Engler said no to a fuel tax hike to support road projects in his state of the state address to the legislature Tuesday evening.
The Republican governor instead proposed a seven-point plan to save more transportation dollars through reforms, greater efficiencies and obtaining more federal money.
Engler's plan would also allocate $70 million for roads this year and another $290 million next year.
None of the road projects would be financed with bonds, according to a spokeswoman for the Michigan Department of Management and Budget.

On the legislative front, Engler vowed to be aggressive in developing and promoting legislation "to fight corruption and assure fairness and integrity" for the casinos voters approved in November for Detroit.
He also proposed a School District Accountability Act that he said would allow state intervention in school districts experiencing high dropout rates or failing test scores.

Declaring Michigan to be "better than ever," Engler said residents would see another $350 million of previously approved tax cuts over the next two years. The state has enacted 21 tax cuts that have totaled more than $6.5 billion so far, he added.
Engler also pointed out that the state's rainy day fund totals $1.1 billion and that the unemployment rate has reached the lowest level since 1969.
"Cutting taxes and controlling state spending have contributed to economic conditions that are the best in three decades," he said.

Engler also made a pitch to work together with what is now a split legislature, with Republicans controlling the Senate and Democrats holding a majority in the House in the wake of the Nov. 5 election.
